questions.question: Evaluate: 32 ÷ 8 x 5 - 2 x 3
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Evaluate: 32 ÷ 8 x 5 - 2 x 3

**Calculation:**

32 ÷ 8 x 5 - 2 x 3

⇒ (32 ÷ 8) x 5 - (2 x 3)

⇒ 4 x 5 - 6

⇒ 20 - 6

⇒ 14

**∴ The correct answer is option (3).**

questions.question: Rakesh sold 154 chairs and had a gain equal to the selling price of 66 chairs. What is his profit percentage?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the Selling Price (SP) of 1 chair be 1 unit.

Total SP of 154 chairs = 154 units, and Gain = SP of 66 chairs = 66 units.

Cost Price (CP) = Total SP − Gain = 154 − 66 = 88 units.

Profit % = (Gain ÷ CP) × 100 = (66 ÷ 88) × 100.

**∴ The correct answer is 75%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total chairs sold = 154

Gain = SP of 66 chairs

**Formula Used:**

SP = CP + Profit

Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

 
 

 CP (88 units)
 Profit (66 units)

 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 Total SP of 154 chairs (154 units)

 Profit % = (66 ÷ 88) × 100 = 75%

**Calculations:**

⇒ SP of 154 chairs = CP of 154 chairs + Gain

⇒ SP of 154 chairs = CP of 154 chairs + SP of 66 chairs

⇒ SP of 154 chairs − SP of 66 chairs = CP of 154 chairs

⇒ SP of 88 chairs = CP of 154 chairs

⇒ Let SP of 1 chair = 1 unit, so CP of 154 chairs = 88 units.

⇒ Gain = SP of 66 chairs = 66 units.

⇒ Profit % = (66 ÷ 88) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (3 ÷ 4) × 100 = 75%

**∴ The correct answer is 75%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Percentage

Profit or Loss percentage is always calculated on the Cost Price (CP) unless specifically stated otherwise in the question. Formula: Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100.

Loss based on SP Concept

If the loss on selling x articles equals the SP of y articles, then the CP of x articles = SP of (x + y) articles. Similarly, if there is a gain, CP of x articles = SP of (x − y) articles.

Dishonest Dealer

When a dealer sells goods at CP but uses a false weight, the Profit % = [Error ÷ (True Value − Error)] × 100.
</p

questions.question: The product of two numbers 5184 and their HCF is 24. What is their LCM?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For any two numbers, LCM = Product of the numbers ÷ HCF

LCM = 5184 ÷ 24

LCM = 216

**∴ The correct answer is 216.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Product of the two numbers = 5184

HCF of the numbers = 24

**Formula Used:**

LCM × HCF = Product of two numbers

**Calculations:**

⇒ LCM × 24 = 5184

⇒ LCM = 5184 ÷ 24

⇒ LCM = 216

**∴ The correct answer is 216.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM and HCF Relationship

For any two given numbers a and b, the product of their HCF and LCM is always equal to the product of the numbers themselves (a × b = HCF × LCM). Note that this rule applies exclusively to exactly two numbers.

Co-prime Numbers

Two numbers are said to be co-prime if their HCF is 1. The LCM of two co-prime numbers is always equal to their direct product.

Fractions Rule

LCM of fractions = LCM of Numerators ÷ HCF of Denominators.
HCF of fractions = HCF of Numerators ÷ LCM of Denominators.
</p

questions.question: The volume of a right circular cone is 168π cm³ and its height is 0.12 m. Find its radius.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Direct formula for the volume of a cone: V = (1/3) × π × r² × h

Convert height to matching units: h = 0.12 m = 12 cm

⇒ 168π = (1/3) × π × r² × 12

⇒ 168 = 4 × r²

⇒ r² = 42 ⇒ r = √42

**∴ The correct answer is √42 cm.**

questions.question: Zakir travels from City A to City B. If Zakir drives his car at (1)/(4) of his normal speed, then he reaches City B 45 minutes late. Find the time (in minutes) that Zakir would have taken to travel from City A to City B if he drove at his normal speed.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Distance is constant, so speed and time are inversely proportional.

Speed ratio (Normal : New) = 4 : 1

Time ratio (Normal : New) = 1 : 4

Difference in time ratio = 4 − 1 = 3 units.

3 units = 45 minutes ⇒ 1 unit = 15 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 15 minutes.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Zakir drives at 1/4 of his normal speed.

He reaches 45 minutes late.

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

When Distance is constant, Speed and Time are inversely proportional.

 
 
 

 
 

 
• 
 
 
 
 City A
 City B
 Distance is Constant

 
 Normal Scenario
 Speed = S, Time = T

 
 New Scenario
 Speed = S/4, Time = 4T

 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 Delay: 4T − T = 45 min

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let his normal speed be S and his normal time be T.

⇒ Normal Distance = S × T

⇒ Under the new condition, his speed becomes S/4.

⇒ New Distance = (S/4) × New Time

⇒ Since distance is the same: S × T = (S/4) × New Time

⇒ New Time = 4T

⇒ Zakir reaches 45 minutes late, which means the difference between the new time and the normal time is 45 minutes.

⇒ 4T − T = 45

⇒ 3T = 45

⇒ T = 45 ÷ 3 = 15

⇒ Normal time taken = 15 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 15 minutes.**

**__Additional Information__**

Proportionality Rules

If distance is constant, speed is inversely proportional to time (S ∝ 1/T). If time is constant, distance is directly proportional to speed (D ∝ S).

Average Speed

For two equal distances covered at speeds x and y, Average Speed = (2xy) ÷ (x + y). This applies when a person travels a specific distance at one speed and returns at another.

Relative Speed

For two bodies moving in opposite directions, relative speed = S₁ + S₂. When moving in the same direction, relative speed = |S₁ − S₂|.
</p

questions.question: In an English exam of 50 marks of a class, 20 students had an average score of 40 marks, 25 students had an average score of 34 marks and 15 students had an average score of 26 marks. What is the weighted average score of the entire class?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of number of students = 20 : 25 : 15 = 4 : 5 : 3 (Total ratio parts = 12)

Let the assumed average be 34.

Net deviation = 4 × (40 − 34) + 5 × (34 − 34) + 3 × (26 − 34)

Net deviation = (4 × 6) + (5 × 0) + (3 × −8) = 24 + 0 − 24 = 0

Actual Average = Assumed Average + (Net Deviation ÷ Total Ratio Parts) = 34 + (0 ÷ 12) = 34

**∴ The correct answer is 34 marks.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of students in group 1 (n₁) = 20, Average score (x₁) = 40

Number of students in group 2 (n₂) = 25, Average score (x₂) = 34

Number of students in group 3 (n₃) = 15, Average score (x₃) = 26

**Formula Used:**

Weighted Average = (n₁x₁ + n₂x₂ + n₃x₃) ÷ (n₁ + n₂ + n₃)

 
 20 Students
 Avg: 40
 
 +
 
 
 25 Students
 Avg: 34

 +
 
 
 15 Students
 Avg: 26

 

 
 
 

 
 

 
 Total 60 Students → Avg: 34

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total marks of group 1 = 20 × 40 = 800

⇒ Total marks of group 2 = 25 × 34 = 850

⇒ Total marks of group 3 = 15 × 26 = 390

⇒ Total marks of all students = 800 + 850 + 390 = 2040

⇒ Total number of students = 20 + 25 + 15 = 60

⇒ Weighted Average = 2040 ÷ 60 = 34

**∴ The correct answer is 34 marks.**

**__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average

Used when different quantities have different weights or frequencies. Formula: Aw = (w₁x₁ + w₂x₂ + ... + wₙxₙ) ÷ (w₁ + w₂ + ... + wₙ).

Net Deviation Method

An assumed mean is chosen to simplify calculations. The actual average equals the assumed mean plus the sum of net deviations divided by the total number of items.
</p

questions.question: Sanjay and Tannu working separately can do a piece of work in 6 and 20 days, respectively. If they work for an alternate day, Tannu beginning, in how many days will the work be completed?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work = LCM(6, 20) = 60 units. Sanjay's efficiency = 10, Tannu's efficiency = 3.

Work in 1 cycle of 2 days (Tannu then Sanjay) = 3 + 10 = 13 units.

Work in 4 cycles (8 days) = 13 × 4 = 52 units, leaving 60 − 52 = 8 units remaining.

On day 9, Tannu completes 3 units. On day 10, Sanjay does the last 5 units in 5 ÷ 10 = 0.5 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 9.5 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Sanjay can do the work in 6 days.

Tannu can do the work in 20 days.

They work on alternate days starting with Tannu.

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 Sanjay
 6
 60
 10
 
 

 Tannu
 20
 3
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Work done in Day 1 by Tannu = 3 units

⇒ Work done in Day 2 by Sanjay = 10 units

⇒ Total work done in 2 days (1 cycle) = 3 + 10 = 13 units

⇒ Work done in 8 days (4 cycles) = 13 × 4 = 52 units

⇒ Remaining work = 60 − 52 = 8 units

⇒ On the 9th day, Tannu works and completes = 3 units

⇒ Remaining work = 8 − 3 = 5 units

⇒ On the 10th day, it is Sanjay's turn. Time taken to complete 5 units = 5 ÷ 10 = 0.5 days

⇒ Total time taken = 8 days + 1 day + 0.5 days = 9.5 days

**∴ The correct answer is 9.5 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Alternate Days Work Concept

When individuals work on alternate days, calculate the combined work of one complete cycle (equal to the number of people). Multiply the cycle to get as close to the total work as possible without exceeding it, then calculate the remaining work day by day in the specific order.

Total Work & Efficiency

Total Work is typically assumed as the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of the individual days taken. Efficiency is the work done per day: Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Days Taken.

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the total work done by each individual. If they work for the same number of days, the wages are divided in the ratio of their efficiencies.
</p

questions.question: Rupali scored twice as many marks in maths as she did in science. Her total marks in maths, science and computer are 234. If the ratio of her marks in maths and computer is 4 ∶ 3. Find Rupali’s marks in maths.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of Maths to Computer = 4 : 3, and Maths is twice Science, so Science ratio = 4 ÷ 2 = 2.

Combined ratio of Maths : Science : Computer = 4 : 2 : 3.

Total ratio units = 4 + 2 + 3 = 9 units.

9 units = 234 marks ⇒ 1 unit = 26 marks.

Maths marks = 4 units × 26 = 104 marks.

**∴ The correct answer is 104 marks.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total marks = 234

Maths marks = 2 × Science marks

Ratio of Maths and Computer marks = 4 : 3

 
 Maths (4x)

 
 Science (2x)

 
 Computer (3x)

 

 
• 
 Total Marks = 9x = 234

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let the marks in Maths and Computer be 4x and 3x respectively.

⇒ Science marks = Maths marks ÷ 2 = 4x ÷ 2 = 2x

⇒ Total marks = Maths + Science + Computer

⇒ 4x + 2x + 3x = 234

⇒ 9x = 234

⇒ x = 234 ÷ 9 = 26

⇒ Marks in Maths = 4x = 4 × 26 = 104

**∴ The correct answer is 104 marks.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Proportion Rule

If two ratios are equal (a : b = c : d), they are in proportion. The product of the extremes equals the product of the means: a × d = b × c.

Combining Ratios

If ratios a : b and b : c are given, multiply the terms so that the common element 'b' has the same value. The combined ratio is then a : b : c.

Distribution of a Quantity

If a total amount T is to be divided in the ratio a : b : c, the share of the first part is calculated as [a ÷ (a + b + c)] × T.
</p

questions.question: The ages of A and B are in the ratio 4 ∶ 9. If the difference of their ages is 10 years, compare their ages after 4 years from now.

Given difference is 10 years, so 5 parts = 10 years ⇒ 1 part = 2 years.

questions.question: The simple interest on a principal amount (in ₹) is ₹387 for a period of 2 years at the rate of 6% per annum. The principal amount (in ₹) is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total interest percentage for 2 years = 6% × 2 = 12%

This 12% corresponds to the Simple Interest of ₹387.

⇒ 1% = 387 ÷ 12 = 32.25

⇒ 100% (Principal) = 32.25 × 100 = 3225

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3225.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 
 Principal (P)

 SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

**Given:**

Simple Interest (SI) = ₹387

Time (T) = 2 years

Rate (R) = 6% per annum

**Formula Used:**

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

**Calculation:**

⇒ 387 = (P × 6 × 2) ÷ 100

⇒ 387 = (P × 12) ÷ 100

⇒ P = (387 × 100) ÷ 12

⇒ P = 38700 ÷ 12

⇒ P = 3225

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3225.**

**__Additional Information__**

Compound Interest (CI)

When interest is compounded annually, Amount A = P(1 + R÷100)T. The compound interest is calculated as CI = A − P.

Difference between CI and SI for 2 years

The difference between Compound Interest and Simple Interest for exactly 2 years is calculated directly as: Difference = P(R÷100)².

Rule of 72

A mental math shortcut used to estimate the number of years required to double the invested principal at a given annual compound rate of return: Years ≈ 72 ÷ Rate.

questions.question: Three-fifth of a journey is covered at a speed of 84 km/hr, and the remaining distance is covered at the rate of 56 km/hr. The average speed for the whole journey (in km/hr) is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the total distance be 5 units, divided into 3 units and 2 units.

Time for the first part = Distance ÷ Speed = 3 ÷ 84 = 1/28 hours.

Time for the remaining part = Distance ÷ Speed = 2 ÷ 56 = 1/28 hours.

Total time taken = 1/28 + 1/28 = 2/28 = 1/14 hours.

Average speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time = 5 ÷ (1/14) = 5 × 14 = 70 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 70 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed for 3/5 of the journey = 84 km/hr

Speed for the remaining journey = 56 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

 
• 
 
• 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 3/5 Distance
 
 

 2/5 Distance
 
 Speed = 84 km/hr
 Speed = 56 km/hr

 Time = (3/5 D) / 84
 Time = (2/5 D) / 56

 Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the total distance of the journey be D.

⇒ Distance covered in the first part = 3D / 5

⇒ Remaining distance = D − (3D / 5) = 2D / 5

⇒ Time taken for the first part = (3D / 5) ÷ 84 = 3D / 420 = D / 140

⇒ Time taken for the remaining part = (2D / 5) ÷ 56 = 2D / 280 = D / 140

⇒ Total time = (D / 140) + (D / 140) = 2D / 140 = D / 70

⇒ Average speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

⇒ Average speed = D ÷ (D / 70) = D × (70 / D) = 70

**∴ The correct answer is 70 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed (General Concept)

Average speed over a journey is defined as the total distance traveled divided by the total time taken, not the simple arithmetic mean of the speeds.

Average Speed (Equal Distances)

If a person covers two equal halves of a journey at speeds x and y, the average speed is given by the formula: (2 × x × y) ÷ (x + y).

Relative Speed

When two bodies move in the same direction at speeds x and y (where x > y), their relative speed is (x − y). If they move in opposite directions, it is (x + y).
</p

Vijay has ₹1218 with him. He divided it amongst his sons Ajay and Prakash and asked them to invest it at 10% rate of interest compounded annually. It was seen that Ajay and Prakash got same amount after 14 and 15 years respectively. How much (in ₹) did Vijay give to Prakash?

**∴ The correct answer is ₹580.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Compound Interest Formula

Amount = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ, where P is the principal sum, R is the rate of interest, and n is the time period in years.

Division of Amount in CI

If a total sum is divided into two parts P₁ and P₂ such that their amounts after t₁ and t₂ years respectively at R% CI are equal, then P₁ / P₂ = (1 + R/100)t² − t¹. The person with less time gets a larger share of the principal.

Simple Interest vs Compound Interest

In Simple Interest, the principal remains constant throughout the period. In Compound Interest, the interest earned in previous periods is added to the principal for the calculation of interest in subsequent periods.

questions.question: What is the effective discount per cent (rounded off to 2 decimal places) if a shopkeeper offers a scheme, “buy five and get one free”?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a “Buy X Get Y Free” scheme, the discount percentage is calculated directly based on the free items.

Effective Discount % = [Free Items ÷ Total Items] × 100

Here, Free items = 1 and Total items = 5 + 1 = 6

⇒ Discount % = (1 ÷ 6) × 100 = 16.666...% ≈ 16.67%

**∴ The correct answer is 16.67%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Scheme: “Buy 5, Get 1 Free”

**Formula Used:**

Discount % = (Discount Amount ÷ Total Marked Price) × 100

 Scheme: Buy 5 Get 1 Free

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the Marked Price (MP) of 1 item be 10 units.

⇒ Total items given to the customer = 5 + 1 = 6 items.

⇒ Total MP of 6 items = 6 × 10 = 60 units.

⇒ The customer only pays for 5 items, so Selling Price (SP) = 5 × 10 = 50 units.

⇒ Discount Amount = Total MP − SP = 60 − 50 = 10 units.

⇒ Effective Discount % = (10 ÷ 60) × 100 = 100 ÷ 6 = 16.666...%

⇒ Rounded off to two decimal places, the discount is 16.67%.

**∴ The correct answer is 16.67%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Buy X Get Y Free

The effective discount percentage is always calculated on the total number of items taken by the customer. Discount % = [Y ÷ (X + Y)] × 100.

Successive Discounts

When two successive discounts of a% and b% are offered, the single equivalent discount is given by: (a + b − ab ÷ 100)%.

Marked Price vs Selling Price

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). The Selling Price (SP) is obtained after subtracting the discount: SP = MP × [(100 − Discount%) ÷ 100].

questions.question: If the selling price of 30 toys is equal to the cost price of 50 toys, then find the gain percentage (round up to two decimal places).
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

If the Selling Price (SP) of x articles is equal to the Cost Price (CP) of y articles, the gain/loss percentage is given directly by the ratio.

Gain % = [(y − x) ÷ x] × 100

Here, x = 30 and y = 50.

Gain % = [(50 − 30) ÷ 30] × 100 = (20 ÷ 30) × 100

Gain % = 66.666... % ≈ 66.67%

**∴ The correct answer is 66.67%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Selling Price of 30 toys = Cost Price of 50 toys

**Formula Used:**

Gain = SP − CP

Gain % = (Gain ÷ CP) × 100

 
 Cost Price = 3 Units
 
 
 Selling Price = 5 Units
 
 
• 
 
• 
 

 

 Profit = 2 Units
 
 Gain % = (2 ÷ 3) × 100 = 66.67%

**Calculations:**

⇒ 30 × SP = 50 × CP

⇒ SP ÷ CP = 50 ÷ 30

⇒ SP ÷ CP = 5 ÷ 3

⇒ Let the Selling Price (SP) be 5 units and Cost Price (CP) be 3 units.

⇒ Gain = SP − CP = 5 − 3 = 2 units

⇒ Gain % = (2 ÷ 3) × 100

⇒ Gain % = 200 ÷ 3

⇒ Gain % = 66.666... % ≈ 66.67%

**∴ The correct answer is 66.67%.**

**__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Fundamentals

Profit occurs when Selling Price > Cost Price. Both Profit and Loss percentages are always calculated on the base of Cost Price unless stated otherwise.

Marked Price and Discount

Discount is offered on the Marked Price (MP) of an item. Selling Price (SP) = Marked Price × (1 − Discount / 100).

Dishonest Dealer Concept

When a dealer sells goods pretending it is at Cost Price but uses a lighter weight, Profit % = [Error ÷ (True Weight − Error)] × 100.
